questions.question: When OSPF learns multiple paths to a network, how does it select a route?

options.text: For each existing interface, it adds the metric from the source router to the destination to calculate the route with the lowest bandwidth.
It counts the number of hops between the source router and the destination to determine the route with the lowest metric.
It divides a reference bandwidth of 100 Mbps by the actual bandwidth of the exiting interface to calculate the route with the lowest cost.
It multiplies the active K values by 256 to calculate the route with the lowest metric.

questions.explanation: OSPF chooses the path with the lowest total OSPF cost. A traditional Cisco default interface cost is reference bandwidth (100 Mb/s by default) divided by interface bandwidth; the reference is configurable.

optionExplanations.A: This does not describe the standardized Cisco OSPF interface-cost calculation.
optionExplanations.B: Hop count is RIP's principal metric, not OSPF's.
optionExplanations.C: OSPF chooses the path with the lowest total OSPF cost. A traditional Cisco default interface cost is reference bandwidth (100 Mb/s by default) divided by interface bandwidth; the reference is configurable.
optionExplanations.D: K values and the EIGRP composite metric belong to EIGRP, not OSPF.

questions.question:
Which attribute does a router use to select the best path when two or more different routes to the same destination exist from two different
routing protocols?
questions.explanation: When equal-length prefixes are learned from different routing protocols, the router compares administrative distances; the lowest distance is preferred before comparing metrics within a protocol.

optionExplanations.A: DUAL is EIGRP's loop-free route computation algorithm, not the interprotocol preference.
optionExplanations.B: Metrics are protocol-specific and normally are not directly compared across different protocols.
optionExplanations.C: When equal-length prefixes are learned from different routing protocols, the router compares administrative distances; the lowest distance is preferred before comparing metrics within a protocol.
optionExplanations.D: Hop count alone is not a universal protocol-selection criterion.

questions.question:
You have configured a router with an OSPF router ID, but its IP address still reflects the physical interface.
Which action can you take to correct the problem in the least disruptive way?
questions.explanation: An OSPF router ID is retained until the OSPF process is restarted. Clearing or restarting the OSPF process can apply the newly configured ID, although it briefly resets adjacencies.

optionExplanations.A: An OSPF router ID is retained until the OSPF process is restarted. Clearing or restarting the OSPF process can apply the newly configured ID, although it briefly resets adjacencies.
optionExplanations.B: Adding a loopback alone does not force an established OSPF process to adopt a new router ID.
optionExplanations.C: A full router reboot is more disruptive than restarting OSPF.
optionExplanations.D: Saving the running configuration does not recalculate the active router ID.

questions.question: Which value is used to determine the active router in an HSRP default configuration?
questions.explanation: With all HSRP routers at the default priority of 100, the highest applicable interface IP address wins the active-router tie-breaker; otherwise priority is compared first.

optionExplanations.A: A loopback is not the usual tie-breaker unless it is the interface address relevant to the group.
optionExplanations.B: With all HSRP routers at the default priority of 100, the highest applicable interface IP address wins the active-router tie-breaker; otherwise priority is compared first.
optionExplanations.C: Priority normally wins, but with untouched default priorities they are tied; IP address breaks that tie.
optionExplanations.D: Object tracking can alter priority but is not the default election tie-breaker.

questions.question: Which configuration command can you apply to a HSRP router so that its local interface becomes active if all other routers in the group fail?
questions.explanation: HSRP automatically elects a surviving standby device to become active when the current active router fails; preempt is used for a higher-priority router to take back the active role.

optionExplanations.A: HSRP automatically elects a surviving standby device to become active when the current active router fails; preempt is used for a higher-priority router to take back the active role.
optionExplanations.B: Tracking reduces an HSRP router's priority when a monitored object fails; it is not needed for basic standby takeover.
optionExplanations.C: Preempt concerns taking over from an existing active router on priority recovery, not ordinary failure takeover.
optionExplanations.D: Increasing priority changes preferred election order but is not required for survivor failover.

questions.question:
R1 has learned route 192.168.12.0/24 via IS-IS, OSPF, RIP, and Internal EIGRP. Under normal operating conditions, which routing protocol is

questions.explanation: For the same prefix, internal EIGRP has the lowest standard administrative distance here: 90 versus OSPF 110, IS-IS 115, and RIP 120.

questions.question:

questions.question:
A packet from a company's branch office is destined to host 172.31.0.1 at headquarters. The sending router has three possible matches in its
routing table for the packet: prefixes 172.31.0.0/16, 172.31.0.0/24, and 172.31.0.0/25. How does the router handle the packet?

options.text: It sends the traffic via prefix 172.31.0.0/24.
It sends the traffic via prefix 172.31.0.0/16.
It sends the traffic via prefix 172.31.0.0/25.
It sends the traffic via the default gateway 0.0.0.0/0.

questions.explanation: Routers use longest-prefix matching. 172.31.0.1 matches /16, /24, and /25, so the /25 route wins regardless of the broader matches.

optionExplanations.A: A matching /24 is less specific than the matching /25.
optionExplanations.B: A matching /16 is much broader than /25.
optionExplanations.C: Routers use longest-prefix matching. 172.31.0.1 matches /16, /24, and /25, so the /25 route wins regardless of the broader matches.
optionExplanations.D: A specific route is available, so the default route is not selected.

To provide end users with a virtual gateway in a multivendor network

questions.question: What does the implementation of a first-hop redundancy protocol protect against on a network?
questions.explanation: FHRPs reduce a LAN's dependence on a single default-gateway router by keeping a virtual gateway reachable if the current active or master device fails.

reach the FULL state?
questions.explanation: Setting ip ospf network point-to-point on a two-router Ethernet link removes unnecessary OSPF DR/BDR elections and treats the connection as point-to-point.

balancing traffic across multiple gateways in proportion to their loads
reduced management overhead on network routers

optionExplanations.C: FHRPs improve default-gateway availability by allowing a backup router to take over the virtual gateway when the current gateway fails.

optionExplanations.A: Both global unicast and unique-local IPv6 addresses use the normal IPv6 prefix-length/subnetting model, even though their routing scopes differ.
optionExplanations.B: Both address types are unicast, not members of the IPv6 multicast group.

questions.question: Which type of IPv4 address type helps to conserve the globally unique address classes?
questions.explanation: RFC 1918 private IPv4 addressing avoids consuming globally unique public space for internal hosts, helping conserve scarce IPv4 addresses.

optionExplanations.B: Multicast addresses identify groups, not private internal host unicast space.
optionExplanations.C: RFC 1918 private IPv4 addressing avoids consuming globally unique public space for internal hosts, helping conserve scarce IPv4 addresses.

questions.question:
When deploying a new network that includes both Cisco and third-party network devices, which redundancy protocol avoids the interruption of

questions.explanation: Standards-based VRRP is interoperable across network equipment vendors and supplies a virtual first-hop gateway, unlike proprietary HSRP on many legacy platforms.

questions.question: What is the role of community strings in SNMP operations?

options.text: It translates alphanumeric MIB output values to numeric values.
It passes the Active Directory username and password that are required for device access.
It serves as a sequence tag on SNMP traffic messages.
It serves as a password to protect access to MIB objects.

questions.explanation: An SNMPv1/v2c community string is a shared access token controlling basic read or write access to MIB objects; it is not encryption or a user account password.

optionExplanations.A: MIB values are decoded by SNMP data types, not translated by community strings.
optionExplanations.B: Active Directory credentials are not what an SNMPv1/v2c community string represents.
optionExplanations.C: A community string is not a packet sequence-number tag.
optionExplanations.D: An SNMPv1/v2c community string is a shared access token controlling basic read or write access to MIB objects; it is not encryption or a user account password.

questions.question: Which syslog severity level is considered the most severe and results in the system being considered unusable?
questions.explanation: Syslog severity 0 is Emergency, meaning the system is unusable; Alert is severity 1, Critical 2, and Error 3.

optionExplanations.A: Error (3) is less severe than Emergency (0), even though it indicates a fault.
optionExplanations.B: Syslog severity 0 is Emergency, meaning the system is unusable; Alert is severity 1, Critical 2, and Error 3.
optionExplanations.C: Alert is severity 1, just below Emergency.
optionExplanations.D: Critical is level 2, below Emergency and Alert.

questions.question:
The clients and DHCP server reside on different subnets. Which command must be used to forward requests and replies between clients on the
10.10.0.1/24 subnet and the DHCP server at 192.168.10.1?

optionExplanations.D: The Cisco IOS ip helper-address command relays client DHCP broadcasts to the specified off-subnet DHCP server.

questions.question: What is the purpose of classifying network traffic in QoS?

options.text: configures traffic-matching rules on network devices
services traffic according to its class
identifies the type of traffic that will receive a particular treatment
writes the class identifier of a packet to a dedicated field in the packet header

questions.explanation: QoS classification recognizes traffic into classes for later queuing, policing, marking, or shaping policy; classification itself need not modify packets.

optionExplanations.A: Traffic-matching rules are a configuration mechanism; classification is the action of identifying the traffic.
optionExplanations.B: Queuing or servicing occurs after classification in the QoS pipeline.
optionExplanations.C: QoS classification recognizes traffic into classes for later queuing, policing, marking, or shaping policy; classification itself need not modify packets.
optionExplanations.D: Marking writes a DSCP/CoS tag, which is a separate possible action after classification.

questions.question: What is the purpose of configuring different levels of syslog for different devices on the network?

options.text: to set the severity of syslog messages from each device
to control the number of syslog messages from different devices that are stored locally
to identify the source from which each syslog message originated
to rate-limit messages for different severity levels from each device

questions.explanation: Syslog severity thresholds determine which classes of events each device sends or records, reducing noise while preserving important diagnostics.

optionExplanations.A: Syslog severity thresholds determine which classes of events each device sends or records, reducing noise while preserving important diagnostics.
optionExplanations.B: Local storage quantity is a possible secondary effect, but severity thresholds classify event importance rather than guarantee a given message count.
optionExplanations.C: Syslog device IDs and facilities identify senders, not per-device severity levels.
optionExplanations.D: Severity levels filter event importance; they do not rate-limit packet/message emission by themselves.

questions.question:
An engineering team asks an implementer to configure syslog for warning conditions and error conditions. Which command does the implementer
configure to achieve the desired result?
questions.explanation: Syslog warning is severity level 4 and errors are level 3; logging trap 4 includes severity 0 through 4.

optionExplanations.A: Severity 5 includes notifications, which is more verbose than the warning/error requirement.
optionExplanations.B: Severity 2 excludes error (3) and warning (4) conditions.
optionExplanations.C: Severity 3 includes error but omits severity-4 warnings.
optionExplanations.D: Syslog warning is severity level 4 and errors are level 3; logging trap 4 includes severity 0 through 4.

questions.question: Which WLC management connection type is vulnerable to man-in-the-middle attacks?
questions.explanation: Telnet sends management credentials and commands without transport-layer encryption and is susceptible to interception; SSH should be preferred.

optionExplanations.A: A direct serial console is local management rather than a remotely intercepted in-band session.
optionExplanations.B: Telnet sends management credentials and commands without transport-layer encryption and is susceptible to interception; SSH should be preferred.
optionExplanations.C: SSH encrypts remote management traffic, unlike Telnet.
optionExplanations.D: HTTPS encrypts HTTP management traffic and is not the insecure method described.

questions.question: What does WPA3 provide in wireless networking?

options.text: backward compatibility with WPA and WPA2
safeguards against brute force attacks with SAE
increased security and requirement of a complex configuration

questions.explanation: WPA3-Personal employs SAE to make offline dictionary attacks on captured password exchanges more difficult than WPA2-PSK.

optionExplanations.A: Transition-mode compatibility can be available in some deployments, but backward compatibility is not WPA3's defining enhanced password defense.
optionExplanations.B: WPA3-Personal employs SAE to make offline dictionary attacks on captured password exchanges more difficult than WPA2-PSK.
optionExplanations.C: WPA3 aims to improve security without making complex configuration an inherent requirement.
optionExplanations.D: Protected Management Frames are mandatory for WPA3, not merely optional.

questions.question: Which global command encrypts all passwords in the running configuration?
questions.explanation: The Cisco IOS global service password-encryption command obfuscates many cleartext passwords appearing in configuration; it is weak reversible encryption, so stronger secret mechanisms remain preferable.

optionExplanations.A: The Cisco IOS global service password-encryption command obfuscates many cleartext passwords appearing in configuration; it is weak reversible encryption, so stronger secret mechanisms remain preferable.
optionExplanations.B: enable password-encryption is not a standard Cisco IOS global command.
optionExplanations.C: enable secret secures only the enable-mode password, not every other line password.
optionExplanations.D: password-encrypt is not the recognized IOS global command.

questions.question: Which type of security program is violated when a group of employees enters a building using the ID badge of only one person?
questions.explanation: Letting multiple people enter a restricted building using one badge is tailgating/piggybacking and violates physical access-control procedures.

optionExplanations.A: Intrusion detection is a technical monitoring function, not badge-sharing entry control.
optionExplanations.B: Logical network authorization does not regulate physical entrance through a door.
optionExplanations.C: Letting multiple people enter a restricted building using one badge is tailgating/piggybacking and violates physical access-control procedures.
optionExplanations.D: User-awareness training can reduce tailgating, but the program being violated is physical access control.

questions.question: Which action must be taken when password protection is implemented?

options.text: Use less than eight characters in length when passwords are complex.
Include special characters and make passwords as long as allowed.
Share passwords with senior IT management to ensure proper oversight.
Store passwords as contacts on a mobile device with single-factor authentication.

questions.explanation: Long, unique passwords with adequate complexity resist guessing better than short passwords; they should never be shared or stored insecurely.

optionExplanations.A: Short passwords remain guessable even if they include some symbol variety.
optionExplanations.B: Long, unique passwords with adequate complexity resist guessing better than short passwords; they should never be shared or stored insecurely.
optionExplanations.C: Sharing passwords with managers undermines individual accountability and secrecy.
optionExplanations.D: A single-factor-protected phone contact list is not a secure credential vault.

questions.question: What is a characteristic of RSA?

options.text: It uses preshared keys for encryption.
It is a private-key encryption algorithm.
It requires both sides to have identical keys.

questions.explanation: RSA is an asymmetric public-key cryptosystem using mathematically related public and private keys; it does not require a single shared encryption key.

optionExplanations.A: RSA relies on asymmetric public and private keys, not a pre-shared symmetric key.
optionExplanations.B: RSA is an asymmetric public-key cryptosystem using mathematically related public and private keys; it does not require a single shared encryption key.
optionExplanations.C: A private key is only one member of RSA's public/private key pair.
optionExplanations.D: Both parties do not use one identical secret key for RSA encryption.

questions.question: What is used as a solution for protecting an individual network endpoint from attack?
questions.explanation: Endpoint antivirus/antimalware software detects and blocks known malicious files and behavior on individual devices; controllers and routers do not replace host protection.

questions.question: Which WPA mode uses PSK authenticaton?

optionExplanations.B: WPA/WPA2-Personal uses a pre-shared key or passphrase; Enterprise mode uses 802.1X/EAP authentication infrastructure instead.

questions.question: Which benefit does Cisco DNA Center provide over traditional campus management?

Cisco DNA Center leverages SNMPv3 for encrypted management, and traditional campus management uses SNMPv2.
Cisco DNA Center leverages APIs, and traditional campus management requires manual data gathering.

questions.question: How does Chef configuration management enforce a required device configuration?

options.text: The Chef Infra Server uses its configured cookbook to push the required configuration to the remote device requesting updates.

questions.question: What describes a northbound REST API for SDN?

options.text: network-element-facing interface for GET, POST, PUT, and DELETE methods
application-facing interface for SNMP GET requests
application-facing interface for GET, POST, PUT, and DELETE methods
network-element-facing interface for the control and data planes

optionExplanations.C: An SDN northbound REST API exposes application-facing resources through HTTP methods such as GET, POST, PUT, and DELETE; southbound APIs target network elements.

It upgrades software and restores files.
It supports distributed processing for configuration.
It provides orchestration and network automation services.

file that defines the target devices upon which commands and tasks are executed
device with Ansible installed that manages target devices
collection of actions to perform on target devices, expressed in YAML format

automatic adjustment of capacity based on need
pooling resources in a multitenant model based on need
self-service of computing resources by the tenant

questions.question: Which QoS feature drops traffic that exceeds the committed access rate?
questions.explanation: Traffic policing enforces a configured rate, commonly dropping or remarking packets over the limit rather than waiting for the rate to decrease.

options.text: It sets QoS attributes within a packet
It modifies the QoS attributes of a packet

It is susceptible to interference from 2.4 GHz devices such as microwave ovens
It is compatible with 802.11b- and 802 11g-compliant wireless devices

questions.question: What is the purpose of an SSID?

It provides CLI access to the network device.
